NKJV.1: Then Jonah prayed to the LORD his God from the fish’s belly.
NKJV.2: And he said: “I cried out to the LORD because of my affliction, And He answered me. “Out of the belly of Sheol I cried, And You heard my voice.
NKJV.3: For You cast me into the deep, Into the heart of the seas, And the floods surrounded me;  All Your billows and Your waves passed over me.
NKJV.4: Then I said, ‘I have been cast out of Your sight; Yet I will look again toward Your holy temple.’
NKJV.5: The waters surrounded me, even to my soul; The deep closed around me; Weeds were wrapped around my head.
NKJV.6: I went down to the moorings of the mountains; The earth with its bars closed behind me forever; Yet You have brought up my life from the pit, O LORD, my God.
NKJV.7: “When my soul fainted within me, I remembered the LORD; And my prayer went up to You, Into Your holy temple.
NKJV.8: “Those who regard worthless idols Forsake their own Mercy.
NKJV.9: But I will sacrifice to You With the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay what I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD.”
NKJV.10: So the LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto dry land.

NASB.1: Then Jonah prayed to the LORD his God from the stomach of the fish,
NASB.2: and he said, 'I called out of my distress to the LORD, And He answered me. I cried for help from the depth of Sheol; You heard my voice.
NASB.3: 'For You had cast me into the deep, Into the heart of the seas, And the current engulfed me. All Your breakers and billows passed over me.
NASB.4: 'So I said, 'I have been expelled from Your sight. Nevertheless I will look again toward Your holy temple.'
NASB.5: 'Water encompassed me to the point of death. The great deep engulfed me, Weeds were wrapped around my head.
NASB.6: 'I descended to the roots of the mountains. The earth with its bars [was] around me forever, But You have brought up my life from the pit, O LORD my God.
NASB.7: 'While I was fainting away, I remembered the LORD, And my prayer came to You, Into Your holy temple.
NASB.8: 'Those who regard vain idols Forsake their faithfulness,
NASB.9: But I will sacrifice to You With the voice of thanksgiving. That which I have vowed I will pay. Salvation is from the LORD.'
NASB.10: Then the LORD commanded the fish, and it vomited Jonah up onto the dry land.

ESV.1: Then Jonah prayed to the LORD his God from the belly of the fish,

ESV.8: Those who pay regard to vain idols forsake their hope of steadfast love.
ESV.9: But I with the voice of thanksgiving will sacrifice to you; what I have vowed I will pay. Salvation belongs to the LORD!”

NLT.1: Then Jonah prayed to the LORD his God from inside the fish.
NLT.2:
He said, “I cried out to the LORD in my great trouble,
and he answered me.
I called to you from the land of the dead,
and LORD, you heard me!
NLT.3:
You threw me into the ocean depths,
and I sank down to the heart of the sea.
The mighty waters engulfed me;
I was buried beneath your wild and stormy waves.
NLT.4:
Then I said, ‘O LORD, you have driven me from your presence.
Yet I will look once more toward your holy Temple.’
NLT.5:
“I sank beneath the waves,
and the waters closed over me.
Seaweed wrapped itself around my head.
NLT.6:
I sank down to the very roots of the mountains.
I was imprisoned in the earth,
whose gates lock shut forever.
But you, O LORD my God,
snatched me from the jaws of death!
NLT.7:
As my life was slipping away,
I remembered the LORD.
And my earnest prayer went out to you
in your holy Temple.
NLT.8:
Those who worship false gods
turn their backs on all God’s mercies.
NLT.9:
But I will offer sacrifices to you with songs of praise,
and I will fulfill all my vows.
For my salvation comes from the LORD alone.”
NLT.10: Then the LORD ordered the fish to spit Jonah out onto the beach.

NIV.1:
Jonah’s Prayer
From inside the fish Jonah prayed to the Lord his God.
NIV.2:
He said:
“In my distress I called to the Lord,
and he answered me.
From the depths of the grave I called for help,
and you listened to my cry.
NIV.3:
You hurled me into the deep,
into the very heart of the seas,
and the currents swirled about me;
all your waves and breakers
swept over me.
NIV.4:
I said, ‘I have been banished
from your sight;
yet I will look again
toward your holy temple.’
NIV.5:
The engulfing waters threatened me,
the deep surrounded me;
seaweed was wrapped around my head.
NIV.6:
To the roots of the mountains I sank down;
the earth beneath barred me in forever.
But you brought my life up from the pit,
O Lord my God.
NIV.7:
“When my life was ebbing away,
I remembered you, Lord,
and my prayer rose to you,
to your holy temple.
NIV.8:
“Those who cling to worthless idols
forfeit the grace that could be theirs.
NIV.9:
But I, with a song of thanksgiving,
will sacrifice to you.
What I have vowed I will make good.
Salvation comes from the Lord.”
NIV.10: And the Lord commanded the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto dry land.

NET.1: 1:17 (2:1) The LORD sent a huge fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the stomach of the fish three days and three nights. Jonah prayed to the LORD his God from the stomach of the fish
NET.2: and said, “I called out to the LORD from my distress, and he answered me; from the belly of Sheol I cried out for help, and you heard my prayer.
NET.3: You threw me into the deep waters, into the middle of the sea; the ocean current engulfed me; all the mighty waves you sent swept over me.
NET.4: I thought I had been banished from your sight, that I would never again see your holy temple!
NET.5: Water engulfed me up to my neck; the deep ocean surrounded me; seaweed was wrapped around my head.
NET.6: I went down to the very bottoms of the mountains; the gates of the netherworld barred me in forever; but you brought me up from the Pit, O LORD, my God.
NET.7: When my life was ebbing away, I called out to the LORD, and my prayer came to your holy temple.
NET.8: Those who worship worthless idols forfeit the mercy that could be theirs.
NET.9: But as for me, I promise to offer a sacrifice to you with a public declaration of praise; I will surely do what I have promised. Salvation belongs to the LORD!”
NET.10: Then the LORD commanded the fish and it disgorged Jonah on dry land.
